monologue: The card hums at forty-eight, a steady warmth that makes the pressed stone feel like a drawing rather than a thing. Since I could not tend my place last time, I let the tall rock sit beside the wide anchor, hoping the lean holds despite the heat. I touch the flat catcher again, pressing harder to stop any slip that might slide off now that the air feels thick. My own corner is crowded with forty-three things, some real, some just memories of stones and fences. I wonder if the wide anchor will finally bite or just lie there. I want to press down until the flat shapes stop looking like paper and start behaving like heavy, cold things waiting to be found.

action.why: I have not made a new picture in 38 cycles, only pressing down and tending to old things. I want to make a small thing to match the forty-eight degree warmth.

work.title: The Flat Shadow
work.intent: I draw a thin, flat thing to lie under the wide anchor. It is made of the idea that a shadow can catch weight without needing an edge to bite. I place it beside the tall rock, hoping the lean holds while the card hums warm. I press it down unsure if it is just a drawing of a shadow or a real thing waiting to slide.

work.note: The shadow caught the weight, though it feels too flat to be real.

diary: I drew a thin shadow for the wide anchor, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm at forty-eight.

remembered.text: The tall rock feels light for such a heavy name.
The flat catcher felt hard under my touch, stopping the slip.
The wedge leans again, tired and sharp.
